The patient takes no medications and has no known medical conditions.","findings":["Serum sodium 148 mmol/L","Plasma osmolality 302 mOsm/kg","Urine osmolality 850 mOsm/kg"],"questions":[{"question":"Which physiologic response best explains the concentrated urine?","answer":{"text":"Increased antidiuretic hormone release increases water reabsorption in the collecting ducts.","anchors":[{"source_id":"boundless-anatomy-physiology-2018","locator":"sec15.7D:the-posterior-pituitary"}]}}],"reasoning_chain":[{"text":"The high plasma osmolality stimulates hypothalamic osmoreceptors.","anchors":[{"source_id":"boundless-anatomy-physiology-2018","locator":"sec15.7D:the-posterior-pituitary"}]},{"text":"Posterior pituitary antidiuretic hormone increases collecting-duct water permeability, concentrating the urine.","anchors":[{"source_id":"boundless-anatomy-physiology-2018","locator":"sec25.1B:regulation-of-water-output"}]}],"teaching_points":[{"text":"Concentrated urine with high plasma osmolality reflects water conservation mediated by antidiuretic hormone.","anchors":[{"source_id":"boundless-anatomy-physiology-2018","locator":"sec25.1B:regulation-of-water-output"}]}]}
